mainTopic: Whether the child of a גוי, an עבד or a half-slave with a בת ישראל is a ממזר, and how immersion done for another purpose can count for conversion or freedom.
overview: The גמרא names רב יהודה as the one who rules that the child of an עבד and a בת ישראל is כשר. It then challenges this with his own ruling that a half-slave's child 'has no fix.' A first answer says that ruling is about a half-slave who made קידושין with her, so his slave side is with an אשת איש. נהרדעי reject this answer: both views learn from אשת אב, and the lenient view says a ממזר comes only from a man whose קידושין can work with other women. So the lenient view permits the child even with a married woman. The גמרא then answers that רב יהודה's case is a half-slave with another man's wife, where his free side makes the child a ממזר. After reports of actual rulings, the הלכה is that the child of a גוי or עבד with a בת ישראל is כשר, whether she was single or married. רבא acts on this rule, and רב יוסף applies it to a woman and her daughter, relying on רב אסי's view that an immersion for נדה counts for conversion. The amud ends with רב's ruling that a slave who immerses first to become free goes free, and the גמרא begins to ask the reason.

steps.title: Identifying who permits the child
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the one who rules the child of a slave and a Jewish woman is כשר is רב יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is he? רב יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the statement before this by naming who holds the lenient view: רב יהודה. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier statement said that whoever is מכשיר with a full slave is also מכשיר with a half-slave. Naming רב יהודה as that person lets the גמרא check this against his other rulings.

phrases.english: Who is he? Rav Yehuda.
phrases.notes: This answers who the 'one who permits' is in the statement just before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the statement from before this section by naming the authority.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה is the one who rules that the child of an עבד and a בת ישראל is כשר.

steps.title: רב יהודה says the half-slave's child has no fix
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רב יהודה saying that the child of a half-slave and a Jewish woman cannot be fixed, which seems to contradict the claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say: if a half-slave half-free man has relations with a Jewish woman, that child has no fix!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim from the step before by pointing to another ruling of רב יהודה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רב יהודה is מכשיר even with a full slave, he should surely be מכשיר with a half-slave. But here he says the half-slave's child 'has no fix', meaning he is a ממזר and cannot marry into the community.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who is half slave and half free
He has no fix, so he cannot marry a regular Jew

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say:

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
phrases.english: one who is half slave and half free
who has relations with a Jewish woman,
that child has no fix!
phrases.notes: He means the child can't marry into the community, like a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the identification of רב יהודה as being lenient with a half-slave.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב יהודה is מכשיר with a half-slave too.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יהודה himself says the half-slave's child has no fix, so he is not lenient here.

steps.title: רב יהודה's ruling is about a half-slave who betrothed her
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's strict ruling is about a case where the half-slave made קידושין with the woman, so his slave side is with a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב יהודה's ruling was said, it was about a case where he betrothed a Jewish woman, so it turns out that his slave side is with a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by limiting רב יהודה's strict ruling to one special case: the half-slave made קידושין with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: קידושין of a slave does not take effect, so she is married only to his free half. When he is with her, his slave half is with an אשת איש, and that is why the child is a ממזר. Without קידושין, רב יהודה would be מכשיר.

phrases.english: When Rav Yehuda's ruling was said,
it was where he betrothed a Jewish woman,
so it turns out that the slave side of him
is having relations with a married woman.
phrases.notes: She is married only to his free half, so to his slave half she is someone else's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the ruling to a specific case (קידושין).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's ruling seemed to cover any half-slave with a Jewish woman.
steps.terutzMaskana: The child is a ממזר only because the slave side is with an אשת איש; otherwise רב יהודה is מכשיר.

steps.title: נהרדעי: the lenient view permits even with a married woman
steps.stepSummary: נהרדעי say in the name of רבי יעקב that whoever is מכשיר is מכשיר even with an אשת איש, which undoes the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the נהרדעי say in the name of רבי יעקב: according to the one who rules the child unfit, he is unfit even with an unmarried woman; according to the one who rules him fit, he is fit even with a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 3 by quoting a rule that the lenient view applies even to a married woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 3 said the child is a ממזר because the slave side is with an אשת איש. But if the מכשיר (like רב יהודה) permits the child of a slave even with a married woman, that reason fails, and the contradiction comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who rules the child unfit
The one who rules the child fit

phrases.english: But didn't the Nehardeans say in the name of Rabbi Yaakov:
according to the one who rules unfit, he rules unfit even with an unmarried woman,

phrases.aramaic: לְדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְשִׁיר — מַכְשִׁיר אֲפִילּוּ בְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
phrases.english: according to the one who rules fit, he rules fit even with a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רב יהודה's ruling is because the slave side is with an אשת איש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מכשיר permits even with an אשת איש, so being with a married woman cannot make the child a ממזר for רב יהודה.

steps.title: Both views learn from a father's wife
steps.stepSummary: Both sides learn from אשת אב; the strict view says wherever קידושין cannot take effect, the child is a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And both of them learned it only from a father's wife. The one who rules unfit holds: just as with a father's wife, where קידושין does not take effect, the child is a ממזר, so too wherever קידושין does not take effect, the child is a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The נהרדעי explain where each view comes from, starting with the strict view. They say both sides build on the law of אשת אב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פוסל compares to אשת אב: קידושין there does not work, and the child is a ממזר. Since קידושין also does not work for a slave or עובד כוכבים, the child is a ממזר even with an unmarried woman. The lenient side's reasoning comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: קידושין does not take effect with her
A child from a forbidden union who cannot marry a regular Jew

steps.confusionAlert: The comparison is not about her being married. It is about קידושין not being able to take effect at all, which is why the strict view applies even to an unmarried woman.

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מֵאֵשֶׁת אָב.
phrases.english: And both of them learned it only from a father's wife.
The one who rules unfit holds:

phrases.aramaic: מָה אֵשֶׁת אָב דְּלָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין
phrases.english: just as a father's wife, with whom betrothal does not take effect,
[the child is a mamzer],
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are added in the corrected wording to finish the thought.

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּל דְּלָא תָּפְסִי בַּהּ קִדּוּשִׁין —
phrases.english: so too anyone with whom betrothal does not take effect,
the child is a mamzer.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם לֹא לְמָדוּהָ אֶלָּא מֵאֵשֶׁת אָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote of the נהרדעי, giving the source for the views they described.
steps.raayaObject: The strict view that the child is a ממזר even with an unmarried woman.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The law of אשת אב: where קידושין does not take effect, the child is a ממזר.

steps.title: The lenient view's reading of אשת אב
steps.stepSummary: The one who rules the child כשר learns from אשת אב only for men whose קידושין can work with other women. A גוי or עבד can never make קידושין, so his child is never a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who rules the child כשר holds: just like אשת אב, where his own קידושין with her does not work but other men's קידושין with her does work, so too here. That leaves out a גוי and an עבד, whose קידושין never works at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof begun in step 5 by giving the lenient side's reading of the אשת אב source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the lenient view, a ממזר comes only from a man who could marry women in general but cannot marry this particular woman, like a son with his father's wife. A גוי or עבד cannot marry any Jewish woman, so he does not fit that pattern, and her being married changes nothing. This shows the lenient view is lenient even with an אשת איש, which knocks down the answer from step 3.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules the child כשר, allowed to marry into the Jewish people

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core reason the lenient view never makes a ממזר from a slave, single woman or married woman. The final הלכה depends on it.

phrases.english: And the one who rules the child fit holds:
Just like one's father's wife,
where for him, betrothal with her does not take effect,
but for others, betrothal with her does take effect,
this excludes a gentile and a slave
for whom betrothal does not take effect at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-sided derivation begun in step 5 and so finishes the attack from step 4 on the answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That the lenient view is lenient even when the woman is married
steps.raayaSupportSource: The derivation from אשת אב, read as applying only where קידושין works with other women

steps.title: A new answer: the half-slave's free side with a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה's strict ruling was about a half-slave who was with a woman married to another man. His free side is with an אשת איש, and that side can make a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רב יהודה's statement was said, it was about a case where the half-slave was with a married woman. It turns out that his free side is being with a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first answer fell, the גמרא gives a new way to explain why רב יהודה said the half-slave's child cannot be fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The slave side of the man would not make a ממזר, as step 6 showed. But his free side is a regular Jewish man who could marry other women, so being with someone else's wife fits the אשת אב pattern and makes a ממזר. So רב יהודה can still hold that a full slave's child is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The free side of a half-slave, half-free man

steps.confusionAlert: In step 3 the woman was the half-slave's own wife, and the problem was his slave side. Now she is another man's wife, and the problem is his free side.

phrases.english: Rather: when Rav Yehuda's statement was said,
it was a case where he was with a married woman,
phrases.notes: "He" is the half-slave, and she is married to some other man.

phrases.english: and it turns out that the free side in him
is having relations with a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer from step 3, which steps 4 to 6 knocked down.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה's ruling was about the half-slave's own wife, with his slave side as the problem.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling is about another man's wife, and the free side makes the ממזר. This fits even the lenient view.

steps.title: Report: רבי יוסי בר אבין ruled lenient for a single woman and strict for a married woman
steps.stepSummary: רבינא reports from רב גזא that רבי יוסי בר אבין ruled the child כשר when the woman was single and פסול when she was married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: רב גזא told me that רבי יוסי בר אבין came to our place. There was a case with a single woman, and he ruled the child כשר. In a case with a married woman, he ruled the child פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shifts from theory to a real-life ruling, reporting what one sage actually did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This report shows a sage who drew a line between the cases: with a single woman the child is כשר, but with a married woman the child is פסול. This is not the strict view from step 5, which is פוסל even with a single woman. It is a middle position that the נהרדעי statement in step 4 rejects. The cases are about a slave or גוי with a Jewish woman.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבִינָא, אָמַר לִי רַב גַּזָּא:
phrases.english: Ravina said: Rav Gazza told me:

phrases.aramaic: אִיקְּלַע רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין לְאַתְרִין
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin happened to come to our place
and there was a case with an unmarried woman, and he ruled the child fit.
With a married woman, he ruled the child unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא אָמַר לִי רַב גַּזָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the theoretical argument to reports of actual rulings.
steps.raayaObject: A distinction: the child is כשר with a single woman but פסול with a married woman
steps.raayaSupportSource: An actual ruling by רבי יוסי בר אבין, as reported by רב גזא

steps.title: Correction: it was רבי יוסי בר זבידא, and he was lenient in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says רב גזא told him a different version. The sage was רבי יוסי בר זבידא, and he ruled the child כשר even with a married woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: רב גזא told me himself that it was not רבי יוסי בר אבין but רבי יוסי בר זבידא, and he ruled the child כשר with both a single woman and a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: A second listener reports the same source differently, which cancels the strict precedent from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both reports come from רב גזא, but רב ששת's version changes both the sage's name and the ruling. In his version the actual ruling followed the lenient view even with a married woman, so step 8 no longer proves that anyone ruled the married-woman case differently in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: To me myself, stressing a firsthand account
Whether... or, meaning in both cases

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לְדִידִי אָמַר לִי רַב גַּזָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said: Rav Gazza told me myself:

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר אָבִין הֲוָה
phrases.english: It was not Rabbi Yosei bar Avin,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי זְבִידָא הֲוָה,
phrases.english: rather, it was Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Zevida,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַכְשַׁר בֵּין בִּפְנוּיָה בֵּין בְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
phrases.english: and he ruled the child fit both with an unmarried woman and with a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת לְדִידִי אָמַר לִי רַב גַּזָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same report and so cancels step 8's strict precedent.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The report in step 8, both the sage's name and the strict ruling
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The report was wrong. The actual ruling was lenient even with a married woman.

steps.title: אמימר also ruled lenient in both cases
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבה tells רבינא that אמימר visited and ruled the child כשר whether the woman was single or married.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא, son of רבה, said to רבינא: אמימר came to our place and ruled the child כשר with both a single woman and a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: Another real-life ruling is reported, adding support for the lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a separate precedent from a different sage, אמימר, and it matches רב ששת's version. Together they point toward the lenient view in practice, which sets up the final הלכה.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa, son of Rabba, said to Ravina:
Ameimar happened to come to our place

phrases.aramaic: וְאַכְשַׁר בֵּין בִּפְנוּיָה בֵּין בְּאֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
phrases.english: and he ruled the child fit both with an unmarried woman and with a married woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה לְרָבִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second lenient precedent that backs step 9.
steps.raayaObject: The lenient view in practice, even with a married woman

steps.title: Final ruling: the child is כשר either way
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה is that when a גוי or עבד is with a בת ישראל, the child is כשר, whether she was single or married.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: if a גוי or an עבד is with a Jewish woman, the child is כשר, whether she was single or married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its final practical ruling, closing the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלכה follows the lenient view from step 6. A גוי or עבד can never make קידושין, so his child cannot be a ממזר, even if the woman was married. The reported rulings of רבי יוסי בר זבידא and אמימר match this.

keyTerms.meaning: The child is fit, not a ממזר

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: the child of a גוי or עבד and a Jewish woman is כשר, even if she was married. Why: a ממזר only comes from a man whose קידושין could work with other women, as with אשת אב. A גוי or עבד cannot make קידושין with any Jewish woman.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל —
phrases.english: And the law is: a gentile or slave who was with a Jewish woman —
the child is fit,
whether she was unmarried or married.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the practical law, following the lenient view and the lenient precedents.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The child of a גוי or עבד with a בת ישראל is כשר, whether she was single or married.

steps.title: רבא declares רב מרי בר רחל fit and appoints him to office
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that רב מרי בר רחל, whose mother was Jewish, is כשר, and he appoints him as an official in Babylonia.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא declared רב מרי בר רחל fit, and he appointed him as one of the officials of Babylonia.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life ruling by רבא that matches the הלכה we just reached. A man whose mother was Jewish was declared fully כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 ruled that the child of a גוי with a בת ישראל is כשר. Here רבא acts on that rule in practice. He even goes one step further and gives this man a position of public authority.

keyTerms.meaning: He declared him fit (כשר), meaning allowed to marry into the Jewish people

phrases.english: Rava declared fit
Rav Mari bar Rachel
and appointed him among the officials of Babylonia,

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אַכְשְׁרֵיהּ לְרַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A practical case that supports the הלכה ruled in step 11
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה that the child of a גוי and a בת ישראל is כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's actual ruling on רב מרי בר רחל, plus his appointment to office

steps.title: Why someone with a Jewish mother counts as 'from among your brethren'
steps.stepSummary: Leaders must come 'from among your brethren,' but because רב מרי's mother was Jewish, he counts as one of the brethren.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though the Master said: 'You shall surely set a king over you' teaches that every appointment you make must be only from among your brethren, this man counts as 'from among your brethren' because his mother is Jewish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a possible problem with רבא's appointment and solves it right away. The פסוק requires leaders to come 'from among your brethren,' and a man with a Jewish mother meets that requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a king is understood to cover every position of authority. One might think a man whose father was not Jewish falls short of 'your brethren.' The answer is that a Jewish mother is enough to place him 'from among your brethren.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'You shall surely set a king over you' (דברים 17:15)
We read it about him, meaning the pasuk's words apply to him

steps.confusionAlert: Being declared כשר to marry and being fit for a position of authority are two separate questions. The גמרא needs an extra reason, the Jewish mother, to explain the appointment.

phrases.english: And even though the Master said:
"You shall surely set a king over you"
all appointments that you make
should be only from among your brethren,
phrases.notes: These words come from the end of the same פסוק.

phrases.english: this one, since his mother is from Israel,
we call him "from among your brethren."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises and resolves a possible objection to רבא's appointment of רב מרי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the person meets the requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A man whose father was not Jewish might not count as 'from among your brethren' and could not hold office
steps.terutzMaskana: A Jewish mother is enough to count as 'from among your brethren'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the child is not only fit to marry. He is also eligible for public leadership.

steps.title: רב יוסף says he can declare a woman and her daughter fit
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אמי's slave immersed a non-Jewish woman to be with her, and רב יוסף says he can declare both her and her daughter כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The slave of רבי חייא בר אמי immersed a certain non-Jewish woman so that she could be with him as a woman. רב יוסף said: I am able to declare both her and her daughter fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case and רב יוסף's bold claim about it. This step sets up the next two steps, which explain each half of his claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The immersion was not done for conversion, so we would expect the woman to still be a non-Jew. Her daughter, whose father is the slave, also seems to have a problem. רב יוסף claims he can solve both problems, and he will explain how in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: For the sake of a woman, meaning so he could be with her, not for conversion

phrases.english: The slave of Rabbi Chiya bar Ami
immersed a certain non-Jewish woman
for the sake of a woman.
phrases.notes: He means she was immersed so he could be with her as a woman, not for the sake of conversion.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
I am able to declare fit
her and her daughter.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַבְדֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַמֵּי אַטְבְּלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case that will again use the הלכה from step 11
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יוסף claims both the woman and her daughter can be declared כשר

steps.title: The mother is fit because her נדה immersion counts
steps.stepSummary: The woman is כשר according to רב אסי, because she immersed for her נדה, and that immersion is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her, I can declare fit according to רב אסי. For רב אסי said: Didn't she immerse for her נדה?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains the first half of his claim, about the mother. He relies on רב אסי's rule that a woman's immersion for נדה can count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that the first immersion was not for conversion. רב אסי teaches that a woman who immerses for נדה, the way Jewish women do, has shown she is joining the Jewish people. So that immersion is enough to make her Jewish.

keyTerms.meaning: Her state of being a נדה (ritually impure from her period)

phrases.english: Her, according to Rav Asi.
For Rav Asi said:
Did she not immerse for her niddah?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first half of רב יוסף's claim (the mother)
steps.raayaObject: The mother is fully Jewish and כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אסי's rule that an immersion for נדה counts

steps.title: The daughter is fit because of the ruling just reached
steps.stepSummary: The daughter is כשר because when a גוי or עבד is with a בת ישראל, the child is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Her daughter, I can declare fit, because when a גוי or an עבד is with a בת ישראל, the child is כשר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains the second half of his claim, about the daughter. He uses the exact הלכה from step 11.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter's father is the slave, and her mother is now treated as Jewish. That fits the rule that the child of an עבד and a בת ישראל is כשר. This ties רב יוסף's case back to the main הלכה, and the next steps go on to tell the stories behind רב אסי's ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה is that the child of a גוי or עבד with a בת ישראל is כשר. רבא and רב יוסף both act on this rule in real cases. A Jewish mother is even enough to count as 'from among your brethren' for holding office.

phrases.english: Her daughter:

phrases.aramaic: גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
phrases.english: a non-Jew or a slave who is with a Jewish woman
the child is fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּבְרַתַּהּ, גּוֹי וְעֶבֶד הַבָּא עַל בַּת יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second half of רב יוסף's claim (the daughter)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The הלכה from step 11 that the child of a גוי or עבד with a בת ישראל is כשר

steps.title: The story behind רב אסי's ruling: the son of the Aramean woman
steps.stepSummary: People called a man 'son of the Aramean woman,' doubting his mother's conversion. רב אסי replied that she surely immersed for her נדה, and that immersion is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man people called 'son of the Aramean woman.' רב אסי said: Didn't she immerse to purify herself from her נדה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells the actual story where רב אסי gave the ruling it already relied on in step 15. A man was being insulted because people doubted his mother's conversion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People doubted whether his mother's conversion immersion was valid. Still, she certainly immersed after her נדה, and רב אסי says that immersion counts. So her conversion is valid and her son is a full Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of the Aramean (non-Jewish) woman. This was an insult hinting that his mother was not truly Jewish.
A woman's state of impurity from her monthly period, which ends with immersion

steps.confusionAlert: רב אסי's question 'Didn't she immerse?' is not a real question. It means 'Of course she immersed, and that is enough!'

phrases.english: There was a certain man whom people would call
"Son of the Aramean woman,"
phrases.notes: This was name-calling. People were hinting that his mother's conversion never really counted.

phrases.english: Rav Asi said:
Didn't she immerse for her menstruation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual story behind רב אסי's ruling, which step 15 used to declare the woman כשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An immersion done for נדה also counts as the immersion for conversion.

steps.title: A matching story: the son of the Aramean man
steps.stepSummary: People called a man 'son of the Aramean man,' doubting his father's conversion. רבי יהושע בן לוי replied that the father surely immersed after a קרי, and that immersion is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a man people called 'son of the Aramean man.' רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Didn't he immerse to purify himself from his קרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, matching story. This time the doubt is about the father, and רבי יהושע בן לוי gives the same kind of answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the male version of רב אסי's idea. A man immerses after a קרי, and רבי יהושע בן לוי says that immersion also counts for conversion. So in both cases an immersion done for another purpose still makes the conversion valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Son of the Aramean (non-Jewish) man. This was an insult about his father's conversion.
A seminal emission, which makes a man impure until he immerses

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב אסי (for a woman's נדה) and רבי יהושע בן לוי (for a man's קרי) hold that an immersion done for purity also counts as the conversion immersion.

phrases.english: There was a certain man whom people would call
"Son of the Aramean man."
Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
Didn't he immerse for his seminal emission?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A matching story to step 17, applying the same idea to a man's father instead of a mother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An immersion done for קרי also counts as the immersion for conversion.

steps.title: A slave bought from a non-Jew who immerses first to become free
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר גוריא quotes רב. If a Jew buys a slave from a גוי, and the slave immerses first with the intent of becoming a free man, the slave goes free.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר גוריא said in the name of רב: Someone bought a slave from a גוי. Before the owner could act, the slave immersed with the goal of becoming a free man. The slave has acquired himself and is free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about immersion. A slave who immerses first, intending to become a free man, frees himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the new Jewish owner would immerse the slave for the sake of עבדות, making him an עבד כנעני. Here the slave got there first and immersed for a different purpose: becoming a full free Jew. רב says the slave's own intention decides the outcome, and he goes free.

keyTerms.meaning: He went first, acting before the owner could
With the intent of becoming a free man
He acquired himself, meaning he is no longer owned

steps.whyThisMatters: This continues the theme of what an immersion accomplishes. Here the slave's own intention while immersing decides whether he becomes a slave or a free Jew.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Gurya said that Rav said:
One who buys a slave from a gentile,
and the slave went first and immersed for the sake of being a free man,
phrases.notes: He immersed before his new owner could immerse him to become a slave.

phrases.english: he has acquired himself as a free man.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from immersion done for another purpose to a new case: a slave immersing on his own to become free.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A slave bought from a גוי who immerses first with the intent of becoming free becomes a free man.

steps.title: Asking for the reason behind רב's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the slave can free himself this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רב's ruling in step 19. This line sets up the answer, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling seems surprising, since the owner paid for the slave. The גמרא wants to know how the slave's own immersion can cancel the owner's purchase.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling in step 19.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a slave who immerses first for freedom becomes free, even though the owner bought him.
